strings.name: William Kentridge
strings.summary: Raised in Johannesburg, Kentridge first studied politics and African studies, then trained in art, mime and theatre. Through charcoal animations repeatedly erased and redrawn, as well as prints, installations and stage works, he examines apartheid, colonial history and the uncertainty of memory. His work circulates through international museums and theatres, often in collaboration with musicians and performers, connecting visual narrative with political experience.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through October 2026; sources checked on 13 November 2026. Stage works involve multiple creators; future touring plans are not treated as completed events.
strings.influence.rationale: Through drawn animation, theatre and installations, he examines South African history and colonial memory, developing an international influence in contemporary art across media.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: BA, University of the Witwatersrand (1976); Johannesburg Art Foundation; École Jacques Lecoq, Paris
strings.highlights.h1.title: Charcoal drawing animation
strings.highlights.h1.text: Erasure and redrawing leave traces of change, bringing personal narratives into dialogue with South African history.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Stage collaboration across media
strings.highlights.h2.text: Combines projection, drawing, music and performance to examine experiences obscured within colonial history.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discusses recent work in an interview
strings.timeline.t1.text: In an interview with Paul Carey-Kent, discussed drawing and recent works, continuing to explain his approach across media.
strings.timeline.t2.title: The Head & the Load premieres
strings.timeline.t2.text: Premiered at Tate Modern, combining music, projection and performance to address African carriers and soldiers in the First World War.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Delivers the Norton Lectures at Harvard
strings.timeline.t3.text: Gave the Charles Eliot Norton Lectures, linking artistic practice with public reflection on seeing, knowledge and creation.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Five Themes exhibited in New York
strings.timeline.t4.text: MoMA surveyed nearly three decades of work in a thematic exhibition emphasizing connections among his media.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Begins a signature animation series
strings.timeline.t5.text: Created Johannesburg, 2nd Greatest City After Paris, exploring South African realities through animated charcoal drawings.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Studies theatre in Paris
strings.timeline.t6.text: Studied mime and theatre at École Jacques Lecoq until 1982, adding training that informed his later stage practice.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Completes university and turns to art
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned a degree in politics and African studies, then trained in fine art at the Johannesburg Art Foundation.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in Johannesburg
strings.timeline.t8.text: Grew up in a family of lawyers opposed to apartheid; attention to institutions, history and politics formed a background to his later work.
